summary: Frontend-only live verification of the 'First-Experience Wave' P2 batch on preview using the fresh throwaway account fresh-p2wave-0903@aurem.dev plus a real-model chat probe on the admin account for the business_voice double-substitution regression check. Most copy/UI changes verified LIVE and PASS. The core business_voice_map fix (P2 bug) does NOT hold up live: a fresh chat message that mentions 'GitHub repo' still produces grammar-mangled output in the reply, and the fresh account's own chat history still shows the exact reported 'your Your website's connection website's pages' string.

critical.issue: REGRESSION NOT FULLY FIXED. Live chat probe on fresh account (fresh-p2wave-0903@aurem.dev) sent 'what can you do with my GitHub repo?' and received a real-model reply containing clearly-broken word-substitution artifacts: 'publish fixes straight to your Website's connection', 'no website's pages is connected to this chat', 'Settings → Website's connection', 'Add website's pages'. The reported fix only added entries for the ADJACENT phrases 'github repo'/'github repository', but individual-word substitutions ('github' → "website's connection", 'repo' → "website's pages") STILL run on words the model uses on their own, producing broken grammar (subject-verb mismatch: 'no website's pages IS connected') and nonsense button labels ('Settings → Website's connection'). Additionally, the fresh account's chat history still displays the pre-fix reply verbatim: 'I can help fix issues in your Your website's connection website's pages—just point me to a problem…' — i.e. the exact double-sub artifact the fix was supposed to eliminate, still user-visible in the UI.

action_items: HIGH — Business voice filter regression is NOT fully fixed. The single-word substitutions 'github' → "website's connection" and 'repo' → "website's pages" produce grammatically-broken output even in replies that DON'T contain the adjacent 'GitHub repo' phrase. Either (a) narrow those single-word entries so they only match in safe contexts, or (b) drop the single-word entries entirely and rely on longer-phrase entries + prompt-side voice guidance. Also: the fresh account's existing chat history still stores the pre-fix double-sub reply — consider whether stored replies need a one-time re-render/back-fill or should just age out.

MEDIUM — P2-F WELCOME greeting could not be verified in a live empty-chat state on the provided fresh account because that account has 2 turns of history already. Either provision a truly-empty account for this round's verification, or add a smoke test that clears history and re-checks the WELCOME bubble.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/config/business_voice_map.json — the SCOPE of the plain-English substitution is too broad. Substituting single tokens like 'github' and 'repo' in ANY position produces broken sentences ('no website's pages is connected', 'Settings → Website's connection'). A word-level replacement filter is a fragile mechanism for non-technical-language rewrites; consider moving voice guidance into the system prompt instead so grammar stays coherent.
ChatPanel.jsx — file continues to grow (>2000 LOC based on browsing). The 'WELCOME' constant is a good candidate to move into a small dedicated module for i18n readiness.

rca of the issue: business_voice_filter.py applies its substitution map to model output post-hoc. The v2026-09-03 map fix added 'github repo' as a longer-phrase entry (matched first) to collapse the adjacent-phrase double-sub, but retained the BARE single-word entries 'github' → "website's connection" and 'repo' → "website's pages". Any reply that mentions 'GitHub' or 'repo' individually (which is common — the model uses these tokens in button labels, subject nouns, prepositional phrases) still gets each token independently rewritten, producing broken grammar ('no website's pages is connected' where the model wrote 'no repo is connected'). Reproduction: log in as fresh-p2wave-0903@aurem.dev, send 'what can you do with my GitHub repo?'. Reply contains 'straight to your Website's connection', 'no website's pages is connected', 'Settings → Website's connection'. Mitigation: either narrow the single-word rules to a specific context (e.g. only when the preceding token is 'your'/'my') or move voice-shaping to system-prompt guidance so the model produces coherent copy natively without a post-hoc regex sweep.
